Change has been successfully merged

You've just linked the schema, you haven't linked where or why this was needed, or the change to the spec that says "all fan sensors shall be percent".  Considering that "percent of what" is VERY subjective on a fan.

Just below this in the commit message I've included the longDescription of the Rotational ReadingType enum. Specifically:

>Services should represent fan speed and pump speed sensors with the `ReadingType` value `Percent`.

This was added to 2025.3

For comparison the v1_11_0 of Sensor does not contain that statement.
```
curl -s https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/Sensor.v1_11_0.json | jq .definitions.ReadingType.enumLongDescriptions.Rotational
"This value shall indicate a measurement of rotational frequency, in revolutions per minute units.  The `ReadingUnits` property shall contain either `{rev}/min`, which is preferred, or `RPM`, which is a deprecated value."
```

This Redfish change was after questions we had on the implementation of SpeedRPM with fan sensors. It was discussed in review comment: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/73700/comments/deae0bcb_0c7ce4e2

Is the enum definition not sufficient in the commit message?
https://github.com/DMTF/Redfish/issues/6197 is the Redfish issue
I've added the links to the Redfish issue and PR with changes for the issue.
Great, that's much better documentation, and now the commit message is self sufficient to describe the change.
Reopening, still need some amount of description of what the user facing upshot is.  "X property is removed, replaced with Y property, and X property changes to Rotational"
I've added summary of difference which will be reflected in response to the commit message. I've also added an example of the unchanged response for clarity.
This seems like it states the opposite of what you're implementing?

My reading of the description is that for non fan speed and pump speed sensors that use Rotational they would use the rev/min or RPM for the ReadingUnits.

But for the exception cases of fan speed and pump speed sensors they should not be using Rotational at all.
I don't think this part is important.. Maybe just remove it and go with the last sentence? Which is the new sentence here..
Done
I've reworded to reference just the added sentence for clarity of why this change is being introduced.
Should we plan to disable first ?
Good point! Updating to default to disabled January 2027 with complete removal by June 2027.
Why are we unpacking the properties AGAIN?  There's already an unpack of these properties in the code you've added this to.

The unpack of these properties is a single one at a time and direct assignment into the JSON. But all three are needed at one time in order to calculate the percent. We also separately unpack properties for determing the Health/Status in the objectPropertiesToJson() function.

I've restructured the flow here and rebased on top of the restructure of objectPropertiesToJson().

Now:
 fillSensorIdentity() will unpack these values as well and pass down to new function convertToFanPercent() to do the conversion work. (I'm keeping a separate getFanPercent() function for unit testing and for eventual use by ThermalMetrics which is not an excerpt, so has different Redfish property names for the same information.)
No, that's not how this works.  if min value isn't published, we either don't publish the property at all or we mark it null.
Modified to match how missing maxValue is handled, so the property won't be published if we cannot compute the percent.
Divide by zero safety issue.
range is computed and checked at L531 above. If it is <= 0 we will return and not do this division.
Shouldn't this be set where we're finding the units on line 617?
Yes that makes more sense. I've moved it into the fillSensorIdentity function path.
This method is already very...very long, lets not make it longer.
I'm working on a separate commit to restructure objectPropertiesToJson() to address this comment. I'll push that separately and rebase on top of it.
Restructure commit: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/85835
Done
These are setting ints, you should probably set floats so they match.
Good catch, I've corrected it.
Ready for re-review.

Does 6 months on enabled make more sense? June / July 2026? 
Just not sure many people are going to do anything until we change the default.
That makes sense. I've changed to disable June 2026 and left removal for another year after that to June 2027.
It looks good to me...with a minor comment

Thank you for the reviews.

I have some questions on some of the comments. Please take a look and let me know how I should proceed on those comments.
A couple of unit tests for this?
I did add unit tests for this function with this commit. Is the comment here that the test are incomplete? Please clarify what cases I missed.
Good point, Ed also had this suggestion. I'll make this change.
Nope, i missed it. Thank you for that.
Done

Can we just return std::optional<double> rather than have an in/out param here?

Should we be rounding this to a sane value?  As written we'll get 1.0000000001 type numbers with lots of precision.  Maybe just return an int and round to the closest percent?

Myung had a similar comment [1]. I'll change the function signature.

So in affect truncate any decimal precision in the result? That seems reasonable. I'll make that change as well.

[1] https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/85103/comment/ca9115b5_2470fe8c/
Yes.  Truncate any precision beyond what we expect.
Done

Does this mean that this gives only the whole interger percent (after truncation)?
What if 
(a) Round up - e.g. 50.9 ==> 60% instead of 50%
(b) Give a 1 or 2 decimal percent (instead of only whole integer percent)?

For (b), I think it may be done by 

```
sensorJson["Reading"] = std::format("{:.2f}", percent);
```

I'm not sure how important the precision is here, especially given that we do report the actual RPM.

(I think when Gunnar and Ed talked to DMTF about this issue [1] they were advocating for being able to just have RPM reported fans and that our use cases don't find percents valuable. That argument was not accepted by DMTF making the conversion to percent necessary.)

[1] https://github.com/DMTF/Redfish/issues/6197

```
inline std::optional<int> getFanPercent(
...
return (((*value - *minValue) * 100) / range);
```
truncates not rounds.. so 33.9% becomes 33%. Rounding might be better.. Return the double or 

```
// Compute fan's RPM Percent value and round off to an int
return static_cast<int>(std::lround(((*value - *minValue) * 100) / range))
```

That said, I could live with truncating
I've changed this to round to the nearest percent. To avoid having to cast I changed the function to return a long instead. I updated the unit test to a case that shows the rounding.

?

0 and 100 are far less confusing than 1E2 and 0E0.

I originally had just 0 and 100 here, but an earlier comment from you [1] indicated that these should match the type. So I changed as above. Is that not what you were looking for?

[1] https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/85103/comment/cc007822_c1445b0b/

Yes, a float would be 100.0 and 0.0 (add the .0 to the end).

With that said, if we're now truncating Reading to an integer, just leave these ints.
Done
Else nullptr?  Reading is a required property, right?

Reading is actually not a required property:

curl -s https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/Sensor.v1_11_1.json | jq .definitions.Sensor.required
[
  "@odata.id",
  "@odata.type",
  "Id",
  "Name"
]

Redfish validator agreed as well. 

That being said, I could make this nullptr if that is preferred.

Yes, it's not technically required, but if we support other properties (RangeMin for example) we're required to support this.

Yes, lets make it nullptr just so we get some indication if something is broken.  From an openbmc perspective we would expect every sensor to have a reading, and a missing reading to be broken software.
Done
These aren't sensor identity parameters.  We already parse these in other code, right?

I agree these are not identity properties.

The MaxValue, MinValue and Value are all needed in order to compute the fan percent value. Originally I had the unpack inside convertToFanPercent() function since they were only needed for that case.


However an earlier comment from you [1] asked for the unpack to be moved with the others.

Additionally an earlier comment from you [2] suggested moving the computing of the fan percent to where we are setting the ReadingType, etc. of the object. So with the restructure I moved it there.

I'm not seeing how I can satisfy both of these comments without organizing the code as it is in this commit. Please let me know if you see a better organization that satisfies these comments.

else?

No else is necessary here. The fan_tach sensor set these to hard-coded values as part of the fillSensorIdentity work. That is what the comment on L875-876 was trying to capture. I'll reword the comment.
I reworded the comment, hopefully it is clearer.

I've addressed the review comments except for the one about the structure of the code. I'm have an outstanding question on that comment. The current structure is what I came up with to address earlier comments. I'm not seeing a different structure that would still address those earlier comments.
We could std::clamp between 0 and 100 but I think that is overkill
Please don't link discussions in a private github as justification for a spec change.  Link the spec, and what it says.

I'm not sure what you are looking for here.


An earlier comment from you asked for more details. I added these two references to the DMTF github to address that comment. You said you liked the updated commit message. [1]

The 2025.3 Overview document does not call out this change.[2] I do have the Schema link in the commit message, which is the most the spec documents it.

I'll remove the PR link from the commit message since that seems to be the line you objected to in this review. But I don't see another reference I can add to the commit message from DMTF that calls out the details of the spec change prompting this bmcweb commit.

Remove the date for changing the default.  That will be a separate discussion.  Also, a date over a year out isn't something we do.

"The code for this option will be removed by the author by June 2026."

I'm confused by the bumping up of the date to remove the option.

The enabled option keeps the prior behavior of reporting the fan_tach sensors as Rotational/RPM and does not do the conversion to percent base. Removing the option and its code would result in removing the old behavior path.

This commit starts with the option enabled to not change existing behavior for any distribution that does not specifically modify a recipe to change the option setting.

So I would expect switching to the new percent base option to be something desired before removing the old code completely. Please advise how you would like this worded.

I changed these to just round to the nearest percent because further precision is not important for our use cases. See earlier comment: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/85103/comment/992bdb6e_5e5c87cf/
